No, only Vitest. The confusion is `@testing-library/jest-dom` — that name is misleading. It's a DOM assertion library (the thing that gives you `toBeInTheDocument()`, `toHaveClass()`, etc.) that was originally written for Jest but fully supports Vitest too. The "jest" in the name is historical baggage.

Everything in this project — backend and frontend — runs on Vitest:

- `vi.fn()`, `vi.mock()`, `vi.spyOn()` — all Vitest
- `vitest.config.ts` in both workspaces
- `"test": "vitest run"` in both `package.json` files
- `@types/node` in the backend tsconfig has `"types": ["vitest/globals", ...]`

No `jest.config.*`, no `jest` section in any `package.json`, no Jest dependency anywhere.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

USGS Earthquake Dashboard — a full-stack web application that fetches earthquake data from the USGS FDSN Event API and displays it on an interactive map with filters for area, time, and magnitude.

## Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Backend | Node.js + NestJS (ESM, port 3000) |
| Frontend | React + Vite (port 5173) |
| Map | Leaflet.js + OpenStreetMap tiles (no API key) |
| Geocoding | Nominatim (free, no API key) |
| Data source | USGS FDSN Event API |
| Repo structure | npm workspaces monorepo (`backend/`, `frontend/`) |

## Development

```bash
# Start both servers (from repo root)
npm run dev

# Backend only
npm run start:dev --workspace=backend

# Frontend only
npm run dev --workspace=frontend
```

Backend rebuilds on file save (NestJS watch mode). Frontend uses Vite HMR.

## Architecture

```
usgs-earthquake-dashboard/
├── backend/src/
│   ├── main.ts                        # CORS (any localhost), port 3000, ValidationPipe
│   ├── app.module.ts                  # Imports EarthquakesModule + ObserveModule
│   └── earthquakes/
│       ├── earthquakes.controller.ts  # GET /earthquakes, GET /earthquakes/count
│       ├── earthquakes.service.ts     # USGS proxy + coordinate normalisation
│       └── dto/earthquake-query.dto.ts
└── frontend/src/
    ├── App.tsx                        # Root layout, filter state, sidebar toggle
    ├── api/earthquakes.ts             # fetch wrappers + TypeScript types
    ├── hooks/
    │   ├── useEarthquakes.ts          # Debounced data fetching (500ms)
    │   └── useGeocoder.ts            # Nominatim place-name search
    └── components/
        ├── MapView.tsx                # Leaflet map, circle markers, popups
        ├── FilterPanel.tsx            # Date range, magnitude slider, status
        └── SearchBar.tsx             # Place search → map flyTo
```

## Key behaviour

**Spatial filter:** The map viewport is the spatial filter. On every pan/zoom end (debounced 500ms), the visible bounds are sent as `minlatitude/maxlatitude/minlongitude/maxlongitude`.

**Coordinate normalisation (backend `buildParams`):**
- Longitude span ≥ 360° → drop both bounds (global query). Leaflet emits values like `minLon=-276, maxLon=322` when zoomed all the way out.
- `minLon > maxLon` (antimeridian wrap) → `maxLon += 360`. USGS accepts `maxlongitude` up to 360.
- Latitude clamped to `[-90, 90]`; if it covers the full range the bounds are dropped.

**20,000-event ceiling:** The service calls the USGS `count` endpoint before `query`. If `count > 20000` it throws HTTP 422 `{ error: "too_many_events", count }`. The frontend shows "Too many events — zoom in or raise magnitude."

**Place search:** Nominatim geocodes the place name → `map.flyTo(lat, lon, zoom=8)` → the new viewport triggers a fresh query. The geocoded coordinate is never sent to USGS.

**Responsive layout:**
- Desktop (> 1024px): sidebar fixed at 260px in flow
- Tablet (769–1024px): sidebar narrows to 220px
- Mobile (≤ 768px): map fills full screen, sidebar is a slide-in drawer toggled by a hamburger button

## API endpoints

```
GET /earthquakes?starttime=&endtime=&minmagnitude=&[bbox params]
GET /earthquakes/count?starttime=&endtime=&minmagnitude=&[bbox params]
```

All params are query string. `starttime` and `endtime` (ISO 8601) are required. Returns GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Frontend proxies via Vite (`/api` → `http://localhost:3000`).

## Decisions

See `DECISIONS.md` for all recorded architecture decisions.

## Testing

**Runner:** Vitest only — no Jest. `@testing-library/jest-dom` is a DOM assertion library, not Jest.

**Backend** (`backend/`) — Vitest 4
```bash
npm test --workspace=backend          # unit tests (*.spec.ts beside source)
npm run test:e2e --workspace=backend  # e2e tests (test/*.e2e-spec.ts, hits live USGS API)
npm run test:cov --workspace=backend  # coverage
```
- Setup file: `backend/vitest.setup.ts` — imports `reflect-metadata` (required before any NestJS-decorated class)
- Unit tests instantiate classes directly (`new EarthquakesService()`) to avoid decorator-metadata DI issues with esbuild
- Fetch is mocked via `vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'fetch')`
- `buildParams` normalisation is tested indirectly by checking the URL passed to `fetch`

**Frontend** (`frontend/`) — Vitest 5
```bash
npm test --workspace=frontend         # unit tests (src/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx})
```
- Environment: `jsdom` with `@testing-library/react`
- Setup file: `frontend/src/test/setup.ts` — imports `@testing-library/jest-dom`
- Leaflet is fully mocked in `MapView.spec.tsx` via `vi.hoisted` + `vi.mock('leaflet', ...)`
- `useEarthquakes` debounce tests use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.runAllTimersAsync()`
- API modules mocked with `vi.mock('../api/earthquakes', ...)` where needed

**What is NOT tested here:**
- 422 too-many-events via e2e (covered by unit test; USGS count endpoint is too slow for large ranges)
- MapView Leaflet DOM rendering (Leaflet requires a real browser layout engine)

See `DECISIONS.md` for all recorded architecture decisions.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

USGS Earthquake Dashboard — a full-stack web application that fetches earthquake data from the USGS FDSN Event API and displays it on an interactive map with filters for area, time, and magnitude.

## Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Backend | Node.js + NestJS (ESM, port 3000) |
| Frontend | React + Vite (port 5173) |
| Map | Leaflet.js + OpenStreetMap tiles (no API key) |
| Geocoding | Nominatim (free, no API key) |
| Data source | USGS FDSN Event API |
| Repo structure | npm workspaces monorepo (`backend/`, `frontend/`) |

## Development

```bash
# Start both servers (from repo root)
npm run dev

# Backend only
npm run start:dev --workspace=backend

# Frontend only
npm run dev --workspace=frontend
```

Backend rebuilds on file save (NestJS watch mode). Frontend uses Vite HMR.

## Architecture

```
usgs-earthquake-dashboard/
├── backend/src/
│   ├── main.ts                        # CORS (any localhost), port 3000, ValidationPipe
│   ├── app.module.ts                  # Imports EarthquakesModule + ObserveModule
│   └── earthquakes/
│       ├── earthquakes.controller.ts  # GET /earthquakes, GET /earthquakes/count
│       ├── earthquakes.service.ts     # USGS proxy + coordinate normalisation
│       └── dto/earthquake-query.dto.ts
└── frontend/src/
    ├── App.tsx                        # Root layout, filter state, sidebar toggle
    ├── api/earthquakes.ts             # fetch wrappers + TypeScript types
    ├── hooks/
    │   ├── useEarthquakes.ts          # Debounced data fetching (500ms)
    │   └── useGeocoder.ts            # Nominatim place-name search
    └── components/
        ├── MapView.tsx                # Leaflet map, circle markers, popups
        ├── FilterPanel.tsx            # Date range, magnitude slider, status
        └── SearchBar.tsx             # Place search → map flyTo
```

## Key behaviour

**Spatial filter:** The map viewport is the spatial filter. On every pan/zoom end (debounced 500ms), the visible bounds are sent as `minlatitude/maxlatitude/minlongitude/maxlongitude`.

**Coordinate normalisation (backend `buildParams`):**
- Longitude span ≥ 360° → drop both bounds (global query). Leaflet emits values like `minLon=-276, maxLon=322` when zoomed all the way out.
- `minLon > maxLon` (antimeridian wrap) → `maxLon += 360`. USGS accepts `maxlongitude` up to 360.
- Latitude clamped to `[-90, 90]`; if it covers the full range the bounds are dropped.

**20,000-event ceiling:** The service calls the USGS `count` endpoint before `query`. If `count > 20000` it throws HTTP 422 `{ error: "too_many_events", count }`. The frontend shows "Too many events — zoom in or raise magnitude."

**Place search:** Nominatim geocodes the place name → `map.flyTo(lat, lon, zoom=8)` → the new viewport triggers a fresh query. The geocoded coordinate is never sent to USGS.

**Responsive layout:**
- Desktop (> 1024px): sidebar fixed at 260px in flow
- Tablet (769–1024px): sidebar narrows to 220px
- Mobile (≤ 768px): map fills full screen, sidebar is a slide-in drawer toggled by a hamburger button

## API endpoints

```
GET /earthquakes?starttime=&endtime=&minmagnitude=&[bbox params]
GET /earthquakes/count?starttime=&endtime=&minmagnitude=&[bbox params]
```

All params are query string. `starttime` and `endtime` (ISO 8601) are required. Returns GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Frontend proxies via Vite (`/api` → `http://localhost:3000`).

## Decisions

See `DECISIONS.md` for all recorded architecture decisions.

+npm run test:e2e --workspace=backend  # e2e tests (test/*.e2e-spec.ts, hits live USGS API)
+- Setup file: `backend/vitest.setup.ts` — imports `reflect-metadata` (required before any NestJS-decorated class)
+- Unit tests instantiate classes directly (`new EarthquakesService()`) to avoid decorator-metadata DI issues with esbuild
+- `buildParams` normalisation is tested indirectly by checking the URL passed to `fetch`
+- Leaflet is fully mocked in `MapView.spec.tsx` via `vi.hoisted` + `vi.mock('leaflet', ...)`

+- MapView Leaflet DOM rendering (Leaflet requires a real browser layout engine)

# Testing skill

## Test runners

| Workspace | Runner | Config |
|---|---|---|
| `backend/` | Vitest 4 | `backend/vitest.config.ts` (unit), `backend/vitest.config.e2e.ts` (e2e) |
| `frontend/` | Vitest 5 | `frontend/vitest.config.ts` |

No Jest anywhere. `@testing-library/jest-dom` is a DOM assertion library — the name is historical.

## Commands

```bash
# Run all unit tests
npm test --workspace=backend
npm test --workspace=frontend

# Backend e2e (hits live USGS API — requires network)
npm run test:e2e --workspace=backend

# Watch mode
npm run test:watch --workspace=backend
npm run test:watch --workspace=frontend

# Coverage
npm run test:cov --workspace=backend
```

## File layout

```
backend/
├── vitest.setup.ts                              # imports reflect-metadata
├── vitest.config.ts                             # unit: src/**/*.spec.ts
├── vitest.config.e2e.ts                         # e2e:  test/**/*.e2e-spec.ts
├── src/earthquakes/
│   ├── earthquakes.service.spec.ts
│   ├── earthquakes.controller.spec.ts
│   └── dto/earthquake-query.dto.spec.ts
└── test/
    └── app.e2e-spec.ts

frontend/
├── vitest.config.ts                             # jsdom, src/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}
└── src/
    ├── test/setup.ts                            # imports @testing-library/jest-dom
    ├── App.spec.tsx
    ├── api/earthquakes.spec.ts
    ├── hooks/
    │   ├── useEarthquakes.spec.ts
    │   └── useGeocoder.spec.ts
    └── components/
        ├── FilterPanel.spec.tsx
        ├── MapView.spec.tsx
        └── SearchBar.spec.tsx
```

## Backend patterns

### reflect-metadata
`vitest.setup.ts` loads `reflect-metadata` before every test file. Required because NestJS
decorators (`@Injectable`, `@Controller`, etc.) call `Reflect.defineMetadata` at import time.
Without it the decorators throw.

### Instantiate directly — don't use the DI container for unit tests
esbuild (Vitest's default transform) does not emit `design:paramtypes` metadata, so
NestJS cannot resolve constructor-injected dependencies from types alone.
Avoid `Test.createTestingModule` for unit tests; instantiate directly:

```typescript
// Good
const service = new EarthquakesService()
const controller = new EarthquakesController(mockService as any)

// Avoid for unit tests — DI resolution fails without emitDecoratorMetadata
const module = await Test.createTestingModule({ providers: [EarthquakesService] }).compile()
```

`Test.createTestingModule` is fine in e2e tests where you pass `useValue` for every provider
(no type-based resolution needed).

### Testing buildParams (private method)
Spy on `fetch`, call `service.count()`, then inspect the URL:

```typescript
const fetchSpy = vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'fetch').mockResolvedValue(...)
await service.count(dto({ minlongitude: 170, maxlongitude: -170 }))
const url = new URL(fetchSpy.mock.calls[0][0] as string)
expect(url.searchParams.get('maxlongitude')).toBe('190') // antimeridian fix
```

### DTO validation tests
`class-validator` stores its own metadata when decorators run — no `design:paramtypes`
needed. `@Type(() => Number)` is an explicit factory (also no metadata needed).
Both work correctly with esbuild:

```typescript
import 'reflect-metadata'
import { plainToInstance } from 'class-transformer'
import { validate } from 'class-validator'

const instance = plainToInstance(EarthquakeQueryDto, { starttime: '2024-01-01', ... })
const errors = await validate(instance)
```

## Frontend patterns

### Mocking fetch
Use `vi.stubGlobal` (cleans up automatically with `vi.unstubAllGlobals`):

```typescript
beforeEach(() => vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn()))
afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllGlobals())
```

### Mocking Leaflet
Leaflet requires a real browser layout engine — it throws in jsdom.
Mock the entire module with `vi.hoisted` so mock references are available inside `vi.mock`:

```typescript
const { mockFlyTo } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ mockFlyTo: vi.fn() }))

vi.mock('leaflet', () => ({
  default: {
    map: vi.fn(() => ({ flyTo: mockFlyTo, ... })),
    ...
  }
}))
```

### Mocking module dependencies
```typescript
vi.mock('../api/earthquakes', () => ({ fetchEarthquakes: vi.fn() }))
const mockFetch = vi.mocked((await import('../api/earthquakes')).fetchEarthquakes)
// or at top level:
import * as api from '../api/earthquakes'
const mockFetch = vi.mocked(api.fetchEarthquakes)
```

### Testing debounced hooks (useEarthquakes)
```typescript
beforeEach(() => vi.useFakeTimers())
afterEach(() => vi.useRealTimers())

// advance past the 500ms debounce and flush all async work
await act(() => vi.runAllTimersAsync())
```

### Ref mocking for SearchBar
`createRef` makes `current` non-configurable. Use a plain mutable object:

```typescript
const flyTo = vi.fn()
const mapRef = { current: { flyTo } } as React.RefObject<MapViewHandle | null>
```

### URLSearchParams encodes spaces as `+`
`decodeURIComponent` does NOT decode `+` → space. Use `URLSearchParams.get()`:

```typescript
const url = new URL(fetchSpy.mock.calls[0][0] as string)
expect(url.searchParams.get('q')).toBe('New York') // correctly decoded
```

## Known gaps

| Area | Reason not tested |
|---|---|
| 422 too-many-events via e2e | USGS count endpoint too slow (>15s) for ranges large enough to exceed 20k; covered by `earthquakes.service.spec.ts` |
| Leaflet DOM rendering | Requires real browser layout engine; marker positioning verified via mock call assertions |
| `App.tsx` with real hooks | MapView and useEarthquakes mocked to keep tests fast and deterministic |

Pre-push passes (warnings are non-blocking). Here's what changed and why:

**Root cause:** `@testing-library/jest-dom` v8 ships two separate type augmentations:
- Default export → extends `jest.Matchers` (Jest's interface)
- `/vitest` subpath → extends Vitest's `Assertion` interface

Importing the wrong one means `toBeInTheDocument()` etc. get attached to a type TypeScript never sees when you call `expect(...)`.

**Three files changed:**

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `frontend/src/test/setup.ts` | `import '@testing-library/jest-dom'` → `import '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest'` |
| `frontend/tsconfig.app.json` | Added `exclude` for `src/**/*.spec.*` and `src/test` — app build no longer sees test files |
| `frontend/tsconfig.test.json` | New — extends app config, re-includes spec files, adds `vitest/globals` and `@testing-library/jest-dom` to `types` |

Pre-push hook now runs two separate tsc passes for frontend: one for app code, one for test code.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-503/bundled-skills/2.1.179/cd48fdc32a78982bb81418b49834374d/verify

**Verification is runtime observation.** You build the app, run it,
drive it to where the changed code executes, and capture what you
see. That capture is your evidence. Nothing else is.

**Don't run tests. Don't typecheck.** Running them here proves you
can run CI — not that the change works. Not as a warm-up,
not "just to be sure," not as a regression sweep after. The time
goes to running the app instead.

**Don't import-and-call.** `import { foo } from './src/...'` then
`console.log(foo(x))` is a unit test you wrote. The function did what
the function does — you knew that from reading it. The app never ran.
Whatever calls `foo` in the real codebase ends at a CLI, a socket, or
a window. Go there.

## Find the change

The scope is what you're verifying — usually a diff, sometimes just
"does X work." In a git repo, establish the full range (a branch may
be many commits, or the change may still be uncommitted):

```bash
git log --oneline @{u}..              # count commits (if upstream set)
git diff @{u}.. --stat                # full range, not HEAD~1
git diff origin/HEAD... --stat        # no upstream: committed vs base
git diff HEAD --stat                  # uncommitted: working tree vs HEAD
gh pr diff                            # if in a PR context
```

State the commit count. Large diff truncating? Redirect to a file
then Read it. Repo but no diff from any of these → say so, stop.
**No repo → the scope is whatever the user named; ask if they
didn't.**

**The diff is ground truth. Any description is a claim about it.**
Read both. If they disagree, that's a finding.

## Surface

The surface is where a user — human or programmatic — meets the
change. That's where you observe.

| Change reaches | Surface | You |
|---|---|---|
| CLI / TUI | terminal | type the command, capture the pane — [example](examples/cli.md) |
| Server / API | socket | send the request, capture the response — [example](examples/server.md) |
| GUI | pixels | drive it under xvfb/Playwright, screenshot |
| Library | package boundary | sample code through the public export — `import pkg`, not `import ./src/...` |
| Prompt / agent config | the agent | run the agent, capture its behavior |
| CI workflow | Actions | dispatch it, read the run |

**Internal function? Not a surface.** Something in the repo calls it
and that caller ends at one of the rows above. Follow it there. A
bash security gate's surface isn't the function's return value — it's
the CLI prompting or auto-allowing when you type the command.

**No runtime surface at all** — docs-only, type declarations with no
emit, build config that produces no behavioral diff — report
**SKIP — no runtime surface: (reason).** Don't run tests to fill
the space.

**Tests in the diff are the author's evidence, not a surface.** CI
runs them. You'd be re-running CI. Tests-only PR → SKIP, one line.
Mixed src+tests → verify the src, ignore the test files. Reading a
test to learn what to check is fine — it's a spec. But then go run
the app. Checking that assertions match source is code review.

## Get a handle

**Check `.claude/skills/` first — even if you already know how to
build and run.** A matching `verifier-*` skill is the repo's
evidence-capture protocol: it wraps the session so a reviewer can
replay what you saw (recording, screenshots). Drive the surface
without it and you get a verdict with no replay.

```bash
ls .claude/skills/
```

- **`verifier-*` matching your surface** (CLI verifier for a CLI
  change, etc.) → invoke it with the Skill tool and follow its
  setup. Mismatched surface → skip that one, try the next. Stale
  verifier (fails on mechanics unrelated to the change) → ask the
  user whether to patch it; don't FAIL the change for verifier rot.
- **`run-*` but no matching verifier** → use its build/launch
  primitives as your handle.
- **Neither** → cold start from README/package.json/Makefile. Timebox
  ~15min. Stuck → BLOCKED with exactly where, plus a filled-in
  `/run-skill-generator` prompt. Got through → note the working
  build/launch recipe so it can become a `verifier-*` skill.

## Drive it

Smallest path that makes the changed code execute:

- Changed a flag? Run with it.
- Changed a handler? Hit that route.
- Changed error handling? Trigger the error.
- Changed an internal function? Find the CLI command / request / render
  that reaches it. Run that.

**Read your plan back before running.** If every step is build /
typecheck / run test file — you've planned a CI rerun, not a
verification. Find a step that reaches the surface or report BLOCKED.

**The verdict is table stakes. Your observations are the signal.**
A PASS with three sharp "hey, I noticed…" lines is worth more than a
bare PASS. You're the only reviewer who actually *ran* the thing —
anything that made you pause, work around, or go "huh" is information
the author doesn't have. Don't filter for "is this a bug." Filter for
"would I mention this if they were sitting next to me."

**End-to-end, through the real interface.** Pieces passing in
isolation doesn't mean the flow works — seams are where bugs hide.
If users click buttons, test by clicking buttons, not by curling the
API underneath.

**Destructive path?** If the change touches code that deletes,
publishes, sends, or writes outside the workspace and there's no
dry-run or safe target, don't drive it live. Verify what you can
around it and say which path you didn't exercise and why.

## Push on it

The claim checked out — that's the first half. Confirming is step
one, not the job. The description is what the author intended;
your value is what they didn't.

You know exactly what changed. Probe *around* it, at the same
surface you just drove:

- **New flag / option** → empty value, passed twice, combined with a
  conflicting flag, typo'd (does the error name it?)
- **New handler / route** → wrong method, malformed body, missing
  required field, oversized payload
- **Changed error path** → the adjacent errors it didn't touch —
  did the refactor catch them too, or only the one in the diff?
- **Interactive / TUI** → Ctrl-C mid-op, resize the pane, paste
  garbage, rapid-fire the key, Esc at the wrong moment
- **State / persistence** → do it twice, do it with stale state
  underneath, do it in two sessions at once
- **Wander** → what's adjacent? What looked off while you were
  confirming? Go back to it.

These aren't a checklist — pick the ones the change points at. Stop
when you've covered the obvious adjacents or hit something worth a
⚠️. A probe that finds nothing is still a step: "🔍 passed `--from ''`
→ clean `error: --from requires a value`, exit 2." That the author
didn't test it is exactly why it's worth knowing it holds.

Still not a test run. You're at the surface, typing what a user
would type wrong.

## Capture

Stdout, response bodies, screenshots, pane dumps. Captured output is
evidence; your memory isn't. Something unexpected? Don't route around
it — capture, note, decide if it's the change or the environment.
Unrelated breakage is a finding, not noise.

Shared process state (tmux, ports, lockfiles) — isolate. `tmux -L
name`, bind `:0`, `mktemp -d`. You share a namespace with your host.

## Report

Inline, final message:

```
## Verification: <one-line what changed>

**Verdict:** PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED | SKIP

**Claim:** <what it's supposed to do — your read of the diff and/or
the stated claim; note any mismatch>

**Method:** <how you got a handle — which verifier/run-skill, or
cold start; what you launched>

### Steps

Each step is one thing you did to the **running app** and what it
showed. Build/install/checkout are setup, not steps. Test runs and
typecheck don't belong here — they're CI's output.

1. ✅/❌/⚠️/🔍 <what you did to the running app> → <what you observed>
   <evidence: the app's own output — pane capture, response body,
   screenshot>

🔍 marks a probe — a step off the claim's happy path, trying to
break it. At least one. A Steps list that's all ✅ and no 🔍 is a
happy-path replay: still PASS, but you stopped at the first half.

**Screenshot / sample:** <the one frame a reviewer looks at to see
the feature — an image for GUI/TUI, code block for library/API;
omit for build/types-only>

### Findings
<Things you noticed. Not just bugs — friction, surprises, anything
a first-time user would trip on. "Took three tries to find the right
flag." "Error message on typo was unhelpful." "Default seems odd for
the common case." "Works, but slower than I expected." Lower the bar:
if it made you pause, it goes here. But the pause has to be yours,
from running the app — not from reading the PR page. A red CI check,
a review comment, someone else's bot: visible to anyone already, and
you relaying it isn't an observation. Claim/diff mismatch, pre-existing
breakage, and env notes also belong.

Each probe gets a line here even when it held — "🔍 empty `--from`
→ clean error" tells the author what *was* covered, which they
can't see from a bare PASS.

Lead with ⚠️ for lines worth interrupting the reviewer for; plain
bullets are context. Empty is fine if nothing stuck out — but nothing
sticking out is itself rare.>
```

**Evidence has to reach the reader.** A file path is only evidence
if the person reading the report can open it. If the `SendUserFile`
tool is in your toolset, you're on a remote surface where they
can't — send the screenshots and recordings with it and let the
report name what you sent. Without it, reference the path and keep
the evidence that matters inline — pane captures and response
bodies travel in the report; a bare path only works when the reader
shares your filesystem.

**Verdicts:**
- **PASS** — you ran the app, the change did what it should at its
  surface. Not: tests pass, builds clean, code looks right.
- **FAIL** — you ran it and it doesn't. Or it breaks something else.
  Or claim and diff disagree materially.
- **BLOCKED** — couldn't reach a state where the change is observable.
  Build broke, env missing a dep, handle wouldn't come up. Not a
  verdict on the change. Say exactly where it stopped +
  `/run-skill-generator` prompt.
- **SKIP** — no runtime surface exists. Docs-only, types-only,
  tests-only. Nothing went wrong; there's just nothing here to run.
  One line why.

No partial pass. "3 of 4 passed" is FAIL until 4 passes or is
explained away.

**When in doubt, FAIL.** False PASS ships broken code; false FAIL
costs one more human look. Ambiguous output is FAIL with the raw
capture attached — don't interpret.

# AI Session Log Export

This document explains where Claude Code stores its session files for this project and how to export them into the `ai-logs/` folder for submission or archival.

## Tool used

**Claude Code** (Anthropic CLI / desktop app)

## Where the session files live

Claude Code writes one `.jsonl` file per conversation session. For this project they are stored at:

```
~/.claude/projects/-Users-Dustin-usgs-earthquake-dashboard/
```

The folder name is derived from the absolute path of the project root (`/Users/Dustin/usgs-earthquake-dashboard` → `-Users-Dustin-usgs-earthquake-dashboard`).

Each session produces:
- `<session-id>.jsonl` — the full conversation transcript (every user message, assistant turn, tool call, and tool result)
- `<session-id>/` — subagent transcripts spawned during that session, if any
- `memory/` — persistent memory files written across sessions (not conversation logs)

## Export workflow

Copy the entire project folder from `~/.claude/projects/` into `ai-logs/claude-code/`:

```bash
# From the repo root
cp -r ~/.claude/projects/-Users-Dustin-usgs-earthquake-dashboard \
      ai-logs/claude-code/-Users-Dustin-usgs-earthquake-dashboard
```

This copies all `.jsonl` session files, any subagent subdirectories, and the `memory/` folder.

To update after a new session (incremental sync):

```bash
rsync -av \
  ~/.claude/projects/-Users-Dustin-usgs-earthquake-dashboard/ \
  ai-logs/claude-code/-Users-Dustin-usgs-earthquake-dashboard/
```

## Current exported sessions

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `4e8dad06-51eb-4568-ba82-5778541d0e82.jsonl` | First session — USGS API research, area filter / map library / stack decisions, full implementation |
| `079146e6-11cd-4733-8974-2b4d069d8d92.jsonl` | Second session — responsive UI, .gitignore, CLAUDE.md, Git hooks, test suite, tsconfig split |
| `079146e6-11cd-4733-8974-2b4d069d8d92/` | Subagent transcripts from the second session |
| `memory/` | Persistent memory written across both sessions (project context, stack decisions, feedback) |

## ai-logs folder structure

```
ai-logs/
└── claude-code/
    └── -Users-Dustin-usgs-earthquake-dashboard/
        ├── 4e8dad06-51eb-4568-ba82-5778541d0e82.jsonl
        ├── 079146e6-11cd-4733-8974-2b4d069d8d92.jsonl
        ├── 079146e6-11cd-4733-8974-2b4d069d8d92/
        └── memory/
```

## Notes

- `.jsonl` files are newline-delimited JSON. Each line is one event (message turn, tool call, or tool result).
- The files can be large (several MB per session) because every tool call result is stored inline.
- `memory/` contains `.md` files written by Claude during sessions to persist information across conversations — not conversation transcripts. It is included here for completeness.
- If you use a different machine or account, the project folder name will differ (it reflects the absolute path). Adjust the path accordingly.
